deck_title: Prandtl-Glauert 1/sqrt(1-M^2) compressible vapor-cone suction vs naive incompressible Bernoulli deficit rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Hermann Glauert (1928) & Ludwig Prandtl (1930) subsonic compressible potential-flow similarity law (streamwise Göthert contraction factor beta = sqrt(1 - M^2) = 1 / (1 + u) and pressure-coefficient amplification C_p(M) = C_p0 / sqrt(1 - M^2) = C_p0 * (1 + u), locking C_p,exact / C_p = 1.0000x across all 17 Mach stations u in [0.000, 1.000] / M in [0.0000, 0.8660] with 0/17 violated) versus naive incompressible Bernoulli pressure coefficient (C_p = C_p0, which underestimates transonic vapor-cone suction by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4 M=0.60, 1.5000x at S8 M=0.75, and 2.0000x at S16 M=0.866 across 16/17 stations) and 64-slice Göthert affine acoustic doublet quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Transonic fighter-jet vapor cones (Prandtl-Glauert condensation clouds), wing-root over-wing fog, and high-speed aerodynamic telemetry shaders
Scaling incompressible baseline pressure coefficients by 1 / sqrt(1 - M^2) so adiabatic expansion cooling crosses the local dew-point threshold at high subsonic Mach
Compressing streamwise wave-packet thickness by beta = sqrt(1 - M^2) as Mach approaches transonic regime
not_for: Hypersonic blunt-body detached bow shocks at M > 5 (where Newtonian sin^2 theta impact theory applies)
Low-speed indoor ceiling fans (M < 0.05 where 1/sqrt(1-M^2) is 1.001)
